summary: ```markdown # CLO2024.2 - Attachment Simulation ## Overview of Improvements In the 2024.2 version, Cloud's component simulation has been improved. The component will now be affected by gravity and the interaction force of the panels. These improvements also enhance the display effect of the component, making it more realistic. Additionally, the stability of the component simulation has been greatly improved. ## Demonstration of Functions We will demonstrate the functions after the improvement through the component on this suit. ### Inserting and Attaching Components First, we insert a component into the object window and attach it to the panel using a glue stick. After that, we adjust its position. When using the right-click unit component, you can see that the simulation options have been increased in the right-click menu. The state of the component simulation is now divided into three states: freeze, activate, and counter-activate. Since the glue tool is used at this time, you can see that the component simulation has been improved. The left-click unit component is unable to switch to freeze or activate states. When you use the right-click unit component to remove the glue, the three simulation states can be switched at this time. Select the activation option and start the simulation. ### Running the Simulation After running the simulation, use the grab tool to drag the component. You will observe that it behaves under the influence of gravity and the interaction force of the panel. The component will fall slightly due to gravity, and the interaction force between the component and the panel will hold it up. The effect of the real component and the panel is consistent, showcasing the realism of the simulation. ## Conflict Thickness and Rigidity Adjustments The right-click component editor has also been added to simulate conflict thickness and rigidity. You can adjust the conflict thickness between the component and the panel by entering a value. In the previous version, components that did not use the glue tool would not be affected by gravity after running the simulation. Therefore, they would remain in their original position and would not fall due to gravity. In the component simulation, the connection can be frozen, allowing it to be fixed to the component, similar to the previous version. ### Freezing Components Let's switch to another component. Right-click the component, choose to freeze, and start the simulation. You will see that the component does not fall under gravity. Using the grab tool to move the component, you can observe the interaction force between the component and the panel. Unlike the activation state, after the component is frozen, you will see that the rigidity in the right attribute editor window is grayed out. This indicates that after freezing, there will be no deformation, and the rigidity of the component cannot be changed. ## Rigidity Settings According to the different types of components, in the 2024.2 version, components will transform based on the interaction force between the component and the panel. First, the component must be in an activated state. Activate the component and check whether the rigidity simulated in the right attribute editor is being utilized. Rigidity refers to the degree of stiffness of the component. The default rigidity of the component is set at 50,000, with a minimum value of 5,000 and a maximum value of 100,000. When we reduce the rigidity of the component to 50,000, and then turn on the simulation, you can see that the component is more likely to be pulled by the power of the panel, resulting in transformation. Conversely, if you want to set it as a solid component that is less likely to transform, you can increase its rigidity. Adjust the rigidity according to the real effect of the component. ### Reverse Activation Simulation Finally, right-click the component, select the reverse activation simulation, and turn on the simulation. The component will remain in its original position. Use your hand to grab the component, and you can see the interaction between the component and the panel, although the interaction effect in the 3D window has disappeared. ## Add-on Simulation From this version onward, the add-on in the 3D window that does not use the glue stick attached to the board can also show the effects of the add-on under the gravity function. First, right-click the add-on and select activate. Then, select the add-on in the object window. Find the option for weight at the bottom of the attribute editor. At this time, the weight of the add-on is 7.6 grams. Simulate to check the effect of the add-on under the current weight. Afterward, change the weight of the add-on to 50 grams, and then simulate again. You will notice that the add-on is more affected by the gravity function. ## Conclusion The above outlines the new functions of our add-on simulation. It should be noted that the current add-on simulation is only suitable for CPU simulation. Based on this, you can set the hardness or weight of the add-on according to the type of add-on you want and adjust it to make the display effect of the add-on simulation more realistic. ```
